title: Command Palette doesn't open when an elevated application is in focus
author: grallbring

status.label: Duplicate known limitation
status.detail: The elevated-foreground activation failure is already tracked in #39704; #45126 was closed as a duplicate after maintainers documented the integrity-level limitation.

next_action.label: Post duplicate response
next_action.reason: Acknowledge the privacy concern and consolidate the known elevation behavior under #39704 without requesting public diagnostics.

judgment.rationale: The exact failure—CmdPal activation while an elevated application has focus—is the subject of open issue #39704 and the detailed maintainer discussion in closed duplicate #45126.
evidence: The reporter reproduced on Windows 11 25H2 with multiple shortcuts and with the low-level hook both enabled and disabled.
The reporter explicitly declined to upload a diagnostic archive because of system-information privacy concerns.
Maintainers explained in #45126 that an unelevated CmdPal low-level hook does not receive input from elevated foreground applications; #45126 was closed as a duplicate of #39704.
judgment.recommended_action: Post a respectful duplicate response linking #39704 and do not ask the reporter to publish a bug-report ZIP.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette activation fails whenever an elevated application owns focus, even after trying alternate shortcuts and hook settings; the reporter is uncomfortable publishing a diagnostic archive.
known_information: PowerToys 0.100.2 was installed from the Microsoft Store on Windows 11 25H2.
The behavior occurs with elevated applications in focus and persists with a non-Windows-key shortcut.
The low-level keyboard hook setting did not change the result.
Open issue #39704 tracks CmdPal activation failure against elevated foreground applications.
inferences: The behavior is consistent with the documented integrity-level isolation of the CmdPal keyboard hook, but the current issue does not independently prove process elevation state for every component.
issue_context.analysis: The supplied evidence already establishes the scenario, and a public diagnostic ZIP is not necessary to decide triage because maintainers have documented and consolidated the same limitation. The appropriate action is deduplication, not another information request.
initial_investigation: Read the full body, both comments, labels, and timeline, including the privacy objection.
Reviewed all 19 comments on #45126; maintainers reproduced the integrity-level behavior and closed it as a duplicate of #39704.
Inspected CmdPalKeyboardService/KeyboardListener.cpp, which installs a WH_KEYBOARD_LL hook inside the CmdPal stack.

actions.label: Post duplicate response

comment.body: Thanks for testing multiple shortcuts and both low-level-hook settings. Your concern about publishing a diagnostic archive is understandable, and no public ZIP is needed to make the triage decision here. This elevated-foreground activation limitation is already tracked in #39704; the same Task Manager/elevation scenario was investigated in #45126 and that issue was closed as a duplicate of #39704. Please continue any additional impact or requirements on #39704 so the work stays consolidated.
